skill.name: ab-test-setup
skill.description: Structured guide for designing valid A/B tests before implementation, with gates for hypotheses, metrics, tracking, and readiness.
skill.summary: Plan rigorous A/B tests with clear hypotheses, metrics, guardrails, sample sizing, and launch readiness checks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All five static alerts are false positives caused by ordinary A/B testing control language. The skill contains only procedural guidance for experiment design, metrics, tracking checks, and result interpretation; no prompt injection, data exfiltration, or reconnaissance intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: Store records in a shared, searchable location to avoid repeated failures.
- Single metric used to evaluate success

finding_verdicts.reason: The line says the workflow blocks invalid hypotheses in an experiment design process. It does not request host details, system commands, or reconnaissance activity.
The line introduces criteria for a valid A/B test hypothesis. It is product experimentation guidance, not system discovery or environment probing.
The line tells the user to choose the simplest valid experiment type. The surrounding content lists A/B test variants and contains no system reconnaissance instructions.
The line recommends storing experiment records in a shared location for organizational learning. It does not instruct file harvesting, credential access, or host enumeration.
The snippet defines a single success metric for an A/B test. It contains no network scanning, endpoint discovery, or external request behavior.

content.value_statement: A/B tests often fail because hypotheses, metrics, and launch criteria are unclear. This skill creates a structured setup workflow with gates for validity and readiness.
actual_capabilities: Guides hypothesis definition with audience, primary metric, expected direction, and MDE.
Checks assumptions about traffic stability, user independence, metric reliability, randomization, and external factors.
Helps select A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, or split URL test types.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics before launch.
Creates readiness gates for tracking verification, sample size, duration, and launch criteria.
Supports disciplined result interpretation and experiment documentation.
limitations: Requires traffic, baseline rate, and metric data from the user.
Does not replace statistical review for high-stakes experiments.
Cannot verify analytics implementation without access to the user system.
Does not automatically run an experiment or deploy variants.

use_cases.title: Product Experiment Planning
use_cases.description: Define a clear hypothesis, audience, metric, and expected effect before a product team designs variants.

use_cases.title: Analytics Readiness Review
use_cases.description: Confirm tracking, attribution, de-duplication, randomization, and guardrail dashboards before launch.

use_cases.title: Growth Test Governance
use_cases.description: Create repeatable gates that prevent peeking, metric changes, and unsupported rollout decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single product experiment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up an A/B test for this change: [describe change]. Ask for any missing hypothesis, audience, baseline, metric, and traffic details.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Hypothesis
prompt_templates.scenario: Review whether an experiment idea is ready for design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this A/B test hypothesis for validity: [hypothesis]. Check audience, evidence, metric, expected direction, and MDE.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Launch Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a readiness checklist before implementation starts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an execution readiness gate for this experiment: [context]. Include metrics, sample size needs, duration, tracking checks, and guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Experiment Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a planned test before launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this complete A/B test plan for validity risks: [plan]. Identify assumption gaps, metric risks, tracking gaps, peeking risks, and stop conditions.

output_examples.input: A product manager wants to test a shorter checkout form but has not chosen a primary metric.
output_examples.output: The skill asks the team to lock a primary metric before variant design, then defines secondary and guardrail metrics for context and safety.

output_examples.input: A data analyst is unsure whether tracking is ready for a signup flow experiment.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a readiness review covering event firing, variant attribution, de-duplication, randomization, and guardrail dashboards.

output_examples.input: A growth team wants to stop a test early after strong first-day results.
output_examples.output: The skill warns against peeking, checks the planned duration and sample size, and recommends waiting unless a guardrail failure occurs.

best_practices: Lock the hypothesis, primary metric, MDE, and audience before creating variants.
Verify tracking and randomization with real event samples before launch.
Document assumptions, results, decisions, and learnings in a shared record.
anti_patterns: Do not change the primary metric after seeing early results.
Do not launch when the baseline rate or traffic level is unknown.
Do not ship a variant that harms guardrail metrics.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create a structured A/B test plan with a hypothesis, metrics, assumptions, sample size needs, tracking checks, and readiness gates.

faq.question: Can it calculate exact sample sizes?
faq.answer: It can guide the required inputs and planning steps, but exact calculations depend on the rates, MDE, power, and tools you provide.

faq.question: Does it support multivariate tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when multivariate testing may fit, while recommending simpler A/B tests when possible.

faq.question: Can it validate analytics tracking directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides verification steps, but your team must check events and dashboards in your analytics tools.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Product managers, data analysts, growth teams, and engineers can use it before implementing or launching experiments.

faq.question: What risks does it reduce?
faq.answer: It reduces invalid hypotheses, weak metrics, premature stopping, poor tracking, and unsupported rollout decisions.
